rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: The vocative is placed between the opening and request to focus attention on the prayer's preamble and intensify its pleading.
rows.anchor: وتوسيط النداء للاهتمام بمقدمة الدعاء زيادة في الضراعة

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: Afʾida is the plural of fuʾād, heart, and here means the self and intellect.
rows.anchor: جمع فؤاد ، وهو القلب . والمراد به هنا النفس والعقل

words: فَٱجْعَلْ أَفْـِٔدَةًۭ مِّنَ ٱلنَّاسِ تَهْوِىٓ إِلَيْهِمْ
rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: The request is that people long to visit the family; mentioning hearts makes their approach seem driven by love and yearning.
rows.anchor: فاجعل أناسا يهوون إليهم . فأقحم لفظ الأفئدة لإرادة أن يكون مسير الناس إليهم

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: Min is explanatory rather than partitive, since restricting the request to only some people would add no useful point.
rows.anchor: بيانية لا تبعيضية ، إذ لا طائل تحته

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: Hawā literally means to fall; here it metaphorically means to move quickly, as in Imruʾ al-Qays's image of a boulder swept down by a torrent.
rows.anchor: وتهوي مضارع هوى بفتح الواو : سقط . وأطلق هنا على الإسراع في المشي

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: Because hawā is used for hurrying toward them, it takes the lām construction here instead of ʿalā.
rows.anchor: ولذلك عدي باللام دون { على .

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: The haste of travel stands metonymically for love and eagerness to visit the family.
rows.anchor: والإسراع : جعل كناية عن المحبة والشوق إلى زيارتهم .

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: The visitors are meant to make the family's home less lonely by coming regularly and meeting their needs.
rows.anchor: والمقصود من هذا الدعاء تأنيس مكانهم بتردد الزائرين وقضاء حوائجهم منهم

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: The indefinite wording is unrestricted, relying on the customary flow of visitors that sustains inhabited towns and markets; abundance need not be stated.
rows.anchor: والتنكير مطلق يحمل على المتعارف في عمران المدن والأسواق بالواردين

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: Love for the family brings affection for the town and repeated visits, making it familiar and encouraging its rites, which advances the religion's call.
rows.anchor: ومحبة الناس إياهم يحصل معها محبة البلد وتكرير زيارته ، وذلك سبب لاستئناسهم به

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: Mentioning gratitude completes the request and adds a prayer that they be grateful; provision should enable worship and remove livelihood's distracting hardship.
rows.anchor: ورجاء شكرهم داخل في الدعاء لأنه جعل تكملة له تعرضا للإجابة وزيادة في الدعاء لهم بأن يكونوا من الشاكرين

words: رَبَّنَآ إِنَّكَ تَعْلَمُ مَا نُخْفِى وَمَا نُعْلِنُ
rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: This turn to God gathers up the preceding account: human misguidance and response, settling Abraham's sons by the House, and prayers for prayer and gratitude.
rows.anchor: جاء بهذا التوجه إلى الله جامعا لما في ضميره ، وفذلكة للجمل الماضية لما اشتملت عليه من ذكر ضلال كثير من الناس

words: إِنَّكَ تَعْلَمُ مَا نُخْفِى وَمَا نُعْلِنُ
rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: The statement teaches Abraham's household and followers that God's knowledge is universal, so they should be watchful in every state and make their intentions sincere.
rows.anchor: وفيه تعليم لأهله وأتباعه بعموم علم الله تعالى حتى يراقبوه في جميع الأحوال ويخلصوا النية إليه

words: وَمَا يَخْفَىٰ عَلَى ٱللَّهِ مِن شَىْءٍۢ فِى ٱلْأَرْضِ وَلَا فِى ٱلسَّمَآءِ
rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: The final clause is a tailpiece explaining that God knows everything; it uses the divine name to stand independently like a comprehensive maxim.
rows.anchor: ولكونها تذييلا أظهر فيها اسم الجلالة ليكون التذييل مستقلا بنفسه بمنزلة المثل والكلام الجامع

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: The clause begins a new sentence but continues Abraham's prayer.
rows.anchor: جملة مستأنفة من تمام دعائه

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: Here ajʿalnī means bring me into that state in the future: make me one who keeps up prayer.
rows.anchor: وفعل { اجعلني } مستعمل في التكوين ، كما تقدم آنفا ، أي اجعلني في المستقبل مقيم الصلاة

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: Iqāma here means continuance or steadfast maintenance, a usage discussed at the beginning of al-Baqara.
rows.anchor: والإقامة : الإدامة ، وتقدم في صدر سورة البقرة .

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: The phrase is an adjective to an omitted noun coordinated with the first-person suffix: make prayer-maintainers among my descendants.
rows.anchor: { ومن ذريتي } صفة لموصوف محذوف معطوف على ياء المتكلم .

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: Min is most plausibly initial, not partitive, since Abraham asks the fullest good for himself and his descendants.
rows.anchor: لأن إبراهيم عليه السلام لا يسأل الله إلا أكمل ما يحبه لنفسه ولذريته

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: A possible partitive reading assumes God had informed Abraham that only some descendants would pray and others disbelieve; Ibn ʿĀshūr calls it weak because the prayer would then seek an accomplished result.
rows.anchor: ويجوز أن تكون { من } للتبعيض بناء على أن الله أعلمه بأن يكون من ذريته فريق يقيمون الصلاة

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: Asking God to accept the prayer is a further act of humble pleading after the preceding supplications.
rows.anchor: ودعاؤه بتقبل دعائه ضراعة بعد ضراعة

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: Most readers omit the final yāʾ in duʿāʾi for lightness; Ibn Kathīr, Abū ʿAmr, and Ḥamza retain it quiescent.
rows.anchor: وحذفت ياء المتكلم في دعاء } في قراءة الجمهور تخفيفا كما تقدم في قوله تعالى :

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: Abraham asks forgiveness for himself, his parents, and believers for what preceded his prophethood and for his father's continued idolatry; his mother may have died before his mission.
rows.anchor: ثم دعا بالمغفرة لنفسه وللمؤمنين ولوالديه ما تقدم منه ومن المؤمنين قبل نبوءته وما استمر عليه أبوه بعد دعوته من الشرك

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: This prayer preceded Abraham's learning that his father was an enemy of God, as stated in Sūrat al-Tawba.
rows.anchor: وهذا الدعاء لأبويه قبل أن يتبين له أن أباه عدو لله كما في آية سورة براءة

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: Qiyām (standing) of the reckoning means its establishment; standing is metaphorically borrowed from a person's strong, active posture.
rows.anchor: ومعنى يقوم الحساب } : يثبت . استعير القيام للثبوت تبعا لتشبيه الحساب

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: The idioms 'war stands on a leg' and 'the sun rises upright' likewise use standing or rising for strength and intensity.
rows.anchor: ومنه قولهم : قامت الحرب على ساق ، إذا قويت واشتدت . وقولهم : ترجلت الشمس

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: This warning follows the reminder that God is not heedless of wrongdoers: the Prophet should take comfort, persist in calling them, and warn them.
rows.anchor: عطف على جملة { ولا تحسبن الله غافلا عما يعمل الظالمون ( إبراهيم : 42 ) ، أي تسل عنهم

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: Al-nās can mean all people, with disbelievers intended by the next clause about the wrongdoers; alternatively it directly denotes the familiar polytheists.
rows.anchor: والناس يعم جميع البشر . والمقصود : الكافرون ، بقرينة قوله : يوم يأتيهم العذاب

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: The day clause is the second object of warn, which takes a second object by extension because the verb includes the sense of cautioning.
rows.anchor: و { يوم يأتيهم العذاب } . منصوب على أنه مفعول ثانن ل { أنذر } ، وهو مضاف

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: Ibn ʿĀshūr cites the hadith that every prophet warned his people of the Dajjāl as a parallel for this extended use of warn.
rows.anchor: كما في الحديث ( ما من نبي إلا أنذر قومه الدجال ) .

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: The 'coming' of punishment is a metonymic expression for its occurrence.
rows.anchor: وإتيان العذاب مستعمل في معنى وقوعه مجازا مرسلا

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: The punishment may be the afterlife's punishment or the worldly punishment with which the polytheists were threatened.
rows.anchor: والعذاب : عذاب الآخرة ، أو عذاب الدنيا الذي هدد به المشركون .

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: Those who did wrong here are the polytheists.
rows.anchor: و { الذين ظلموا } : المشركون .

words: رَبَّنَآ أَخِّرْنَآ إِلَىٰٓ أَجَلٍۢ قَرِيبٍۢ نُّجِبْ دَعْوَتَكَ وَنَتَّبِعِ ٱلرُّسُلَ
rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: If the punishment is in the afterlife, they ask to defer judgment and return to worldly life to answer God's call, as in the plea in 23:99–100; the messengers are all who brought God's call.
rows.anchor: فالتأخير بمعنى تأخير الحساب ، أي يقول الذين ظلموا : أرجعنا إلى الدنيا لنجيب دعوتك . وهذا كما في قوله تعالى

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: If they speak at the onset of worldly punishment, delay is literal and 'the messengers' is a singular used figuratively for Muḥammad.
rows.anchor: وإن حمل على عذاب الدنيا فالمعنى : أن المشركين يقولون ذلك حين يرون ابتداء العذاب فيهم .

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: Qarīb means a short span: time is likened to distance, and they ask for only enough time to answer the call.
rows.anchor: والقريب : القليل الزمن . شبه الزمان بالمسافة ، أي أخرنا مقدار ما نجيب به دعوتك

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: Because the preceding clause reports their plea, the following words give its answer through an implied 'it is said to them'; reproach rejects the request.
rows.anchor: لما ذكر قبل هذه الجملة طلب الذين ظلموا من ربهم تعين أن الكلام الواقع بعدها يتضمن الجواب

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: The answer turns from direct acceptance or refusal to an interrogative rebuke, which itself entails refusal.
rows.anchor: وقد عدل عن الجواب بالإجابة أو الرفض إلى التقرير والتوبيخ لأن ذلك يستلزم رفض ما سألوه .

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: The opening conjunction hints at an omitted clause refusing their plea: 'No! Had you not sworn…'; the refusal is shortened because the reprimanded do not get their wish.
rows.anchor: التقدير كلا وألم تكونوا أقسمتم

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: Zawāl means moving from a place and here means leaving the graves for the reckoning.
rows.anchor: والزوال : الانتقال من المكان . وأريد به هنا الزوال من القبور إلى الحساب .

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: The omitted complement of 'departure' is clear from the context; compare the oath that God will not resurrect the dead.
rows.anchor: وحذف متعلق { زوال } لظهور المراد ، قال تعالى : { وأقسموا بالله جهد أيمانهم لا يبعث الله من يموت

words: أَقْسَمْتُم مِّن قَبْلُ مَا لَكُم مِّن زَوَالٍۢ
rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: The second clause explains their oath without an implied quotation; it keeps second-person address rather than switching to 'we have no departure.'
rows.anchor: وجملة ما لكم من زوال } بيان لجملة { أقسمتم } . وليست على تقدير قول محذوف

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: The oath may have been made by all wrongdoers in earthly life, as polytheist generations received the same teachings from predecessors.
rows.anchor: وهذا القسم قد يكون صادر من جميع الظالمين حين كانوا في الدنيا لأنهم كانوا يتلقون تعاليم واحدة في الشرك

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: Alternatively, most or some members of those peoples swore it, while the others held the same meaning implicitly.
rows.anchor: ويجوز أن يكون ذلك صادرا من معظم هذه الأمم أو بعضها ولكن بقيتهم مضمرون لمعنى هذا القسم

words: وَسَكَنتُم فِى مَسَٰكِنِ ٱلَّذِينَ ظَلَمُوٓا۟ أَنفُسَهُمْ
rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: The address covers all polytheist peoples except the first, since the earliest people could not have inhabited the dwellings of earlier polytheists.
rows.anchor: وكذلك الخطاب في قوله : { وسكنتم في مساكن الذين ظلموا أنفسهم } فإنه يعم جميع أمم الشرك عدا الأمة الأولى

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: Sakan here means to occupy or settle in a place, explaining the use of fī although the verb ordinarily takes a direct object.
rows.anchor: والمراد بالسكنى : الحلول ، ولذلك عدي بحرف الظرفية خلافا لأصل فعله المتعدي بنفسه .

words: وَسَكَنتُم فِى مَسَٰكِنِ ٱلَّذِينَ ظَلَمُوٓا۟ أَنفُسَهُمْ
rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: Arab travelers on routes to Syria and Yemen passed through Thamūd's and ʿĀd's lands and stopped there.
rows.anchor: وكان العرب يمرون على ديار ثمود

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: The peoples saw what God had done to their predecessors by observing the traces of punishment, including destruction and annihilation.
rows.anchor: وتبين ما فعل الله بهم من العقاب حاصل من مشاهدة آثار العذاب من خسف وفناء استئصال

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: The clause may coordinate one report with another or describe the people addressed by 'warn the people' while they plot.
rows.anchor: يجوز أن يكون عطف خبر على خبر ، ويجوز أن يكون حالا من { الناس } في قوله : { وأنذر الناس }

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: Makr is secretly planning and harboring an evil act against another; Ibn ʿĀshūr cites its use in 3:54 and 7:99.
rows.anchor: تبييت فعل السوء بالغير وإضماره

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: The first makr is a cognate accusative specifying the kind of plotting; its annexed pronoun names the plotters, as does the second makr.
rows.anchor: لبيان النوع ، أي المكر الذي اشتهروا به

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: ʿInda Allāh may mean in God's knowledge, warning of accountability, or God's creative determination of the recompense for their plot.
rows.anchor: فهو تعري بالوعيد والتهديد

words: وَإِن كَانَ مَكْرُهُمْ لَتَزُولَ مِنْهُ ٱلْجِبَالُ
rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: The majority read the lām in litazūla with kasra and the verb in subjunctive, making in negative and the lām a lām al-juhūd.
rows.anchor: وقرأ الجمهور { لتزول } بكسر اللام وبنصب الفعل المضارع بعدها فتكون ( إن ) نافية ولام { لتزول } لام الجحود

words: وَإِن كَانَ مَكْرُهُمْ لَتَزُولَ مِنْهُ ٱلْجِبَالُ
rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: On the majority reading, their plot cannot move mountains; the belittling comparison implies the Prophet and believers stand firm like mountains.
rows.anchor: وهو استخفاف بهم ، أي ليس مكرهم بمتجاوز مكر أمثالهم ، وما هو بالذي تزول منه الجبال

words: وَإِن كَانَ مَكْرُهُمْ لَتَزُولَ مِنْهُ ٱلْجِبَالُ
rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: Al-Kisāʾī alone reads the first lām with fatḥa and the verb with nominative, taking in as a lightened emphatic particle distinguished from negation by the lām.
rows.anchor: وقرأ الكسائي وحده بفتح اللام الأولى

words: وَإِن كَانَ مَكْرُهُمْ لَتَزُولَ مِنْهُ ٱلْجِبَالُ
rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: On al-Kisāʾī's reading their plot is hyperbolically powerful enough to move mountains if mountains could move; 19:90 uses a similar exaggeration.
rows.anchor: فيكون الكلام إثباتا لزوال الجبال من مكرهم ، أي هو مكر عظيم لتزول منه الجبال لو كان لها أن تزول

words: وَقَالُوا۟ يَٰٓأَيُّهَا ٱلَّذِى نُزِّلَ عَلَيْهِ ٱلذِّكْرُ
rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: This is conjoined to the command to leave them in 15:3: that clause depicts indulgence and hopes, while this depicts deeper disbelief and denial of Muḥammad's message.
rows.anchor: والمناسبة أن المعطوف عليها تضمنت انهماكهم في الملذات والآمال

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: The sense is to leave them to disbelieve and say all manner of things in denial and mockery.
rows.anchor: والمعنى : ذرهم يكذبون ويقولون شتى القول من التكذيب والاستهزاء .

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: The whole sentence is presented as the polytheists' own speech.
rows.anchor: والجملة كلها من مقولهم

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: The vocative publicly spotlights the description; the relative clause is selected because they pretend that revelation is grounds for mockery, as the insult that follows shows.
rows.anchor: لما في الصلة من المعنى الذي جعلوه سبب التهكم

rows.speaker: النبي صلى الله عليه وسلم
rows.claim: The Prophet told ʿĀʾisha that God diverted the polytheists' abuse: they insulted Mudhammam while he was Muḥammad.
rows.anchor: فقال النبي صلى الله عليه وسلم لعائشة : ( ألم تري كيف صرف الله عني أذى المشركين وسبهم ، يسبون مذمما وأنا محمد )

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: The relative clause attributes the description to the referent according to what those using the title claim, not according to the speaker's own belief; this is mockery.
rows.anchor: وفي هذا إسناد الصلة إلى الموصول بحسب ما يدعيه صاحب اسم الموصول ، لا بحسب اعتقاد المتكلم على طريقة التهكم .

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: Dhikr can mean verbal utterance or recollection; the revealed speech is called dhikr because it is recited and repeated, reminds of God and the Last Day, or gives later generations a remembrance of them.
rows.anchor: فالذكر الكلام الموحى به ليتلى ويكرر

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: Calling the Qur'an dhikr is a remarkably comprehensive naming that Arabs had not known before its appearance in the Qur'an.
rows.anchor: فتسمية القرآن ذكرا تسمية جامعة عجيبة لم يكن للعرب علم بها من قبل أن ترد في القرآن

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: Qurʾān names the revelation for its intended recitation; dhikr and qurʾān name forms of discourse meant for people's reception and recitation, like poetry, sermons, stories, and fables.
rows.anchor: وكذلك تسميته قرآنا لأنه قصد من إنزاله أن يقرأ ، فصار الذكر والقرآن صنفين من أصناف الكلام الذي يلقى للناس

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: The verse begins by refuting their mockery in 15:6, after the answer to their challenge to produce angels in 15:7; the two replies are unfolded in reverse order.
rows.anchor: استئناف ابتدائي لإبطال جزء من كلامهم المستهزئين به ، إذ قالوا : { يأيها الذي نزل عليه الذكر

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: The reply uses their own premise—affirming that the Reminder was sent to the Messenger—to silence their ridicule, and stresses the true statement with inna and the separating pronoun, as in 63:1.
rows.anchor: وكان هذا الجواب من نوع القول بالموجب بتقرير إنزال الذكر على الرسول مجاراة لظاهر كلامهم . والمقصود الرد عليهم في استهزائهم

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: The parenthetical second clause escalates the rebuke: the sender of the Reminder himself preserves it; the wāw is parenthetic and the pronoun refers to the Reminder.
rows.anchor: بأن منزل الذكر هو حافظه من كيد الأعداء

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: The lām strengthens the verb's effect because the verb comes after its object.
rows.anchor: واللام لتقوية عمل العامل لضعفه بالتأخير عن معموله

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: Preservation includes preventing the Reminder from vanishing, being added to or diminished, or being altered; God facilitated mass transmission and memorization from the Prophet's lifetime.
rows.anchor: وشمل حفظه الحفظ من التلاشي ، والحفظ من الزيادة والنقصان فيه ، بأن يسر تواتره وأسباب ذلك ، وسلمه من التبديل والتغيير

rows.speaker: القاضي إسماعيل بن إسحاق بن حماد المالكي البصري
rows.claim: As related by Qāḍī ʿIyāḍ, Ismāʿīl ibn Isḥāq explained that earlier books changed because God entrusted their scholars with preservation, whereas God preserves the Qur'an himself.
rows.anchor: أن القاضي إسماعيل بن إسحاق بن حماد المالكي البصري سئل عن السر في تطرق التغيير للكتب السالفة

rows.speaker: أبو الحسن بن المنتاب
rows.claim: Abū al-Ḥasan ibn al-Muntāb repeated Ismāʿīl's explanation to al-Muḥāmilī, who replied that no statement could be better.
rows.anchor: قال أبو الحسن بن المنتاب ذكرت هذا الكلام للمحاملي فقال لي : لا أحسن من هذا الكلام

rows.speaker: سفيان بن عيينة
rows.claim: A report in al-Qurṭubī, attributed there to Yaḥyā ibn Aktham, recounts Sufyān ibn ʿUyayna saying prior scripture was entrusted to its people and lost, while God guards the Qur'an so it is not lost.
rows.anchor: وفي تفسير ( القرطبي ) في خبر رواه عن يحيى بن أكثم : أنه ذكر قصة إسلام رجل يهودي في زمن المأمون

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: Ibn ʿĀshūr suggests the parallel explanations may be a coincidence of independent thoughts.
rows.anchor: ولعل هذا من توارد الخواطر

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: The promise honors the Qur'an and angers the polytheists by announcing that the religion will prevail and the Qur'an endure through the ages.
rows.anchor: وفي هذا مع التنويه بشأن القرآن إغاظة للمشركين بأن أمر هذا الدين سيتم وينتشر القرآن ويبقى على ممر الأزمان

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: Its endurance is a challenge and sign of the Messenger's truth: a human composition or non-miracle would admit corruption and contradiction, unlike the Qur'an (4:82).
rows.anchor: وهذا من التحدي ليكون هذا الكلام كالدليل على أن القرآن منزل من عند الله آية على صدق الرسول صلى الله عليه وسلم

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: This follows the preservation answer to the mockery of 15:6 and refutes it by comparing the scoffers with earlier nations.
rows.anchor: باعتبار أن تلك جواب عن استهزائهم في قولهم

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: The analogy with earlier peoples confirms the scoffers' disbelief, implicitly threatens them, and consoles the Messenger.
rows.anchor: وفي هذا التنظير تحقيق لكفرهم لأن كفر أولئك السالفين مقرر عند الأمم ومتحدث به بينهم . وفيه أيضا تعريض بوعيد أمثالهم

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: The lām of oath and qad stress that God sent messengers before, matching the sending they denied and found astonishing, as in 10:2.
rows.anchor: والتأكيد بلام القسم و ( قد ) لتحقيق سبق الإرسال من الله ، مثل الإرسال الذي جحدوه واستعجبوه

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: Shiyaʿ is the plural of shīʿa, a group united in one matter; it means the communities or generations of ancient peoples.
rows.anchor: وهي الفرقة التي أمرها واحد

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: The phrasing refers to ancient communities, some of which received messengers and others of which did not.
rows.anchor: أي في أمم الأولين ، أي القرون الأولى فإن من الأمم من أرسل إليهم ومن الأمم من لم يرسل إليهم .

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: Kāna marks the scoffing as their settled habit, and the imperfect verb indicates that it recurred.
rows.anchor: و { كانوا به يستهزءون } يدل على تكرر ذلك منهم وأنه سنتهم ، ف ( كان ) دلت على أنه سجية لهم

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: The object of arsálnā is omitted, but the verb form and the following mention of a messenger make 'messengers' understood.
rows.anchor: ومفعول { أرسلنا } محذوف دلت عليه صيغة الفعل ، أي رسلا ، ودل عليه قوله : { من رسول }

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: Fronting the prepositional phrase before 'they mock' restricts their activity hyperbolically, as if mocking the messenger were all they did.
rows.anchor: وتقديم المجرور على { يستهزءون } يفيد القصر للمبالغة ، لأنهم لما كانوا يكثرون الاستهزاء برسولهم وصار ذلك سجية لهم

words: فَإِذَا سَوَّيْتُهُۥ وَنَفَخْتُ فِيهِ مِن رُّوحِى
rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: The account of Adam is conjoined to another narrative; the opening idh is governed by an omitted 'remember,' as in parallel passages in al-Baqara and al-Aʿrāf.
rows.anchor: مفعول لفعل ( اذكر ) محذوف

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: Bashar is synonymous with insān, meaning a human being.
rows.anchor: الإنسان ، أي أني خالق إنسانا

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: The angels either understood human nature through knowledge God imparted to them or through God's description of it in a comprehensive formulation.
rows.anchor: بما ألقى الله فيهم من العلم

words: فَإِذَا سَوَّيْتُهُۥ وَنَفَخْتُ فِيهِ مِن رُّوحِى
rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: Specifying the human's material teaches that a creature's honor comes from its qualities, not the substance from which it is composed.
rows.anchor: وإنما ذكر للملائكة المادة التي منها خلق البشر ليعلموا أن شرف الموجودات بمزاياها لا بمادة تركيبها

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: Taswiya is adjustment of a thing's constitution; here it is the balancing and completion of its elements until it can receive the spirit.
rows.anchor: على اعتدال العناصر فيه واكتمالها بحيث صارت قابلة لنفخ الروح

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: Blowing literally expels compressed air between pursed lips; here it metaphorically denotes the sudden placement of a subtle, powerfully acting force, with no actual blowing or blown object.
rows.anchor: استعير هنا لوضع قوة لطيفة السريان قوية التأثير دفعة واحدة

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: As an approximation, life involves a rapidly formed vaporous or electrical force from the heart at the completion of bodily temperament, whose effects flow through arteries throughout the body.
rows.anchor: وتقريب نفخ الروح في الحي أنه تكون القوة البخارية أو الكهربائية المنبعثة من القلب عند انتهاء استواء المزاج وتركيب أجزاء المزاج

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: Attributing the blowing and spirit to God's pronoun honors this creature.
rows.anchor: وإسناد النفخ وإضافة الروح إلى ضمير اسم الجلالة تنويه بهذا المخلوق

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: The passage implies that elements are distinguished before God by their effects and actions; human notions of dirtiness or purity reflect sensory response, temperament, or custom.
rows.anchor: وفيه إيماء إلى أن حقائق العناصر عند الله تعالى لا تتفاضل إلا بتفاضل آثارها وأعمالها

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: After evidence that God alone creates and that this entails benefaction and gratitude, the two clauses draw the conclusion and rebuke the polytheists.
rows.anchor: على انفراد الله بالخلق ابتداء من قوله تعالى

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: The rhetorical question denies any equality between creator and noncreator; the comparison targets the polytheists' treatment of idols as God's partners and shows who merits divinity.
rows.anchor: أي لا يستوي من يخلق بمن لا يخلق

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: Since the noncreators meant are idols, the normally rational relative pronoun man is used by matching the wording of man who creates.
rows.anchor: وحين كان المراد بمن لا يخلق الأصنام كان إطلاق من الغالبة في العاقل مشاكلة لقوله أفمن يخلق

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: The question rebukes the polytheists for turning away instead of reflecting on the denied equality.
rows.anchor: مستعمل في الإنكار على انتفاء التذكر

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: The statement that God's blessings cannot be counted completes the preceding argument by generalizing its evidence of benefaction and grounds for gratitude.
rows.anchor: وهي كالتكملة لها لأنها نتيجة لما تضمنته

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: This comprehensive reminder says God's blessings are so numerous that no counter can enumerate them, as seen in their basic sources and the worlds they contain.
rows.anchor: وهذا كلام جامع للتنبيه على وفرة نعم الله تعالى على الناس بحيث لا يستطيع عدها العادون

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: The uncountable blessings imply abundant gratitude, expose the enormity of ingratitude, and intensify the threat to the ungrateful.
rows.anchor: تعريض بفظاعة كفر من كفروا بهذا المنعم

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: The closing assurance of forgiveness and mercy lets them repent of idolatry and prepare to give thanks; Qur'anic warnings are followed by encouragement lest sinners despair.
rows.anchor: تنبيها على تمكنهم من تدارك أمرهم

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: This clause is conjoined to the denial of equality in 16:17 and to the statement in 16:19 that God knows what people conceal.
rows.anchor: وجملة والله يعلم ما تسرون

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: Those invoked besides God are the idols; the address here focuses on the polytheists, a subset of the earlier addressees.
rows.anchor: ظاهر أن الخطاب هنا متمحض للمشركين وهم بعض المخاطبين

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: This passage explicitly states the idols' lack of creative power and knowledge, which the preceding arguments had already implied.
rows.anchor: والمقصود من هذه الجملة التصريح بما استفيد ضمنا مما قبلها وهو نفي الخالقية ونفي العلم عن الأصنام

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: The denial that idols create anything makes explicit the implication of the earlier question about creator and noncreator.
rows.anchor: استفيد من جملة { أفمن يخلق

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: Saying that they themselves are created advances the proof against their divinity.
rows.anchor: ارتقاء في الاستدلال على انتفاء إلهيتها

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: The implied creator is God: idols are made of stones created by Him, and human carving does not change that origin, as 37:96 says.
rows.anchor: فإنهم من الحجارة التي هي من خلق الله

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: Calling the idols dead makes explicit what the statement that God knows what people conceal implied, by denying knowledge through the absence of its prerequisite, life.
rows.anchor: بطريقة نفي الشيء بنفي ملزومه

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: Lack of life entails lack of knowledge, and inability to know their own state entails inability to know others'; such beings cannot be gods.
rows.anchor: يستلزم نفي العلم عنها لأن الحياة شرط في قبول العلم

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: The phrase 'not living' reinforces 'dead,' making clear there is no trace of life in them because they are stones.
rows.anchor: للدلالة على عراقة وصف الموت فيهم بأنه ليس فيه شائبة حياة لأنهم حجارة

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: Stones can be described as dead because death is simply absence of life; privative descriptions need not denote something capable of a positive state, despite logicians' convention.
rows.anchor: ولا يشترط في الوصف بأسماء الأعدام قبول الموصوفات بها
